meta.title: Code Heros — the programmers who build a hundred applications

hero.name: Code Heros
hero.tagline: The programmers who build a hundred applications.
hero.lede: Code Heros is a public list of programmers who have a hundred public repositories of their own, every one of them real code. The bar to join is ten. Ten public repositories put a name on the list; the count beside it runs to a hundred. Anyone can check an entry, and anyone can add one with a pull request.

items.name: A hundred public repositories of your own
items.body: Public: anyone can open, read and clone the repository. Your own: you created it. A fork of someone else's repository is theirs, not yours, and does not count.

items.name: Each one real code
items.body: Ten commits or more, and more than a hundred lines of code in a programming language. A repository that is only a README, or only prose, data or configuration, does not count, and is left out of the hundred. Stars are not asked for.

heroes.title: Code Heros
heroes.none: There is no hero of 100 applications yet!

join.title: Add yourself
join.lede: The list lives in a GitHub repository, and an entry is one pull request.

steps.name: One file
steps.body: Add data/heros/<handle>.json: your name, your links, and at least ten applications, each with its public repository.

steps.name: Pull request
steps.body: Open a pull request. A check runs on it: the file parses, there are ten applications, every repository answers. The rest is read by a person.

join.language: The list is written in English. Where a description carries a translation, the page shows it in the reader's language.
join.collected: Not every entry is written by the person it names. The people who keep the site also collect entries themselves, and those are checked and corrected the same way as any other.
join.prompt: Or copy the prompt, give it to an AI assistant with a GitHub profile, and it writes the file.
